scope: Proposition 3.7 (Polar-part bounds) of the manuscript “Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic” (preprints/Abundance-in-numerical-dimension-one-for-terminal-threefolds-in-positive-characteristic-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 035 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e170f2c29b7026e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be a semistable vector bundle of slope zero. For every integer i, h0( V, G(iD) ) ≤ rk G, h0( V, G⊗2 (iD) ) ≤ (rk G)2 . (3.10) For each fixed bundle J = G or J = G⊗2, the increasing spaces H0( V, J(iD)/J ) , i = 1, 2, . . . , (3.11) have bounded dimension and eventually stabilize under their natural injections. In particular their elements have a uniform bound on their actual pole orders along every prime component of D. This pole bound may depend on J; it is uniform in the cut i and in the chosen section.
